Hi everybody,

As I am new to this forum I would like to take a moment to introduce myself first.

When I started about 25 years ago to sculpt, I was amazed by the 3D aspect of the things, later on I got familiar to digitals-sculpting (computer generated objects), lenticular and stereoscopic imaging. For now I am experimenting to find my way combining these techniques together.

If you could give a night vision to a Neanderthal man he would have felt and reacted like me when I saw a hologram for the first time!

But it seemed to be so complicated and far away that I could not imagine to have the possibilities one day to do it myself.

Finally about 6 months ago I decided to start to learn the basics of holography.

Here is my approach so far, for those (like myself 6 months ago) who want to start but don’t know how and where to begin.

After a long research I ordered a kit and some materials from “Integraf” what I strongly recommend to every beginner like myself. Their kit is very useful and most important of all they provide a perfect service and feedback and all that with care and sympathy.

I have also carefully read the famous book of “Practical Holography”

In the meantime I search and read again and again what I could find about Holography, lasers and…on the internet.

One of the members of this forum “Kris Meerlo” has been a great help, informing and advising me by e-mail and therefore I am very grateful to him.

Here I’m now wondering if I can get some advise and help to buy professional materials?

Here are my questions:

1/ If you could go back in time and start again knowing that you can invest 300$-350$ for a laser what would be your choice?

P.S. Considering the unstability of my working environment (second floor, old house…) I have to minimize the exposure time, therefore it’s important that the laser provides at least 20-30 mW of output power.

After days of research and with my poor knowledge on the subject I have found some options:

a- The D&S LASERS driver unit of Mr. Frank DeFreitas with the 35mW Hitachi AlGalnP Laser Diode that he proposes. (I know that Colin has one, are you satisfy with it?)

b- One of these: [http://www.laser.sk/EN/KOMPONENTY/diodovemod.htm](http://www.laser.sk/EN/KOMPONENTY/diodovemod.htm) they sell also a laser diode module LM Ø14 (40mW) 650 for something like 150$.

c- Or 30mW(90$) [http://www.lasershow.sk/diodovemod.php](http://www.lasershow.sk/diodovemod.php)

d- I found some green laser modules here: [http://www.z-bolt.com](http://www.z-bolt.com) (green DPSS laser modules) they have also a pulsed green laser-pointer: [http://www.z-bolt.com/btg---6p.htm](http://www.z-bolt.com/btg---6p.htm) I don’t have any idea of their stability and their degree of what you call mode hopping ; Is 30 pulses per second convenient for holography?

2/ Are all the spatial filters so expensive or I’m not looking for the right thing!?

Those I have found cost at least 300$, does anyone know where I can get a secondhand one?

I thank you all for this nice forum, it is wonderful to find a place where enthusiastic guys like you share the same patient.

My excuses for this long message.

posts.content_md: If you have an old microscope or can purchase one cheap that has an x-y transitional stage to move the glass slide in the x-y direction then you can very easily make your own precision spatial filter. The mircoscope already comes with the correct threading for the objective and the focus is your z axis movement. Then simply mount a pinhole on the x-y transitional stage. posts.author: Dinesh
posts.content_md:
The thing to look for in a laser are: power, coherence length and polarisation.

The power may or may not have to be as high as you may think, depending on the setup and surroundings. On the other hand, the more the better. Michael shoots on the second floor and gets pretty good results. The key is in making a good vibration isolation table, surrounding it with a screen to block out outside and airborne noises and having black cards to break up air currents on the table surface. Also note the traffic flow and aircraft activity in your area. Most holographers work late at night to minimise disturbance from traffic. Before you build your table, it's best to check various areas of the room you propose to build the table with a michaelson interferometer on the floor. While a Michaelson on a floor will never give steady fringes, it'll give you an idea of where your room is the most stable. There are lots of threads on the forum on getting mirrors and a home-made beamsplitter.

The coherence length determines the depth you can shoot. If you're making a single beam Denisyuk (object behind plate and beam hitting the front of the film), the coherence length needs to be the distance from the film to the back of the object and back to the film. When you go on to split beam setups, the coherence length just determines the deepest object you can shoot. I'm not too knowledgeable on DPSS laser and diode lasers, but I believe a well tuned DPSS can give you many feet of coherence, so this may not be the problem. Typically a coherence length of about 6 inches (15cm) is a good distance for simple Denisyuks. If and when you buy a laser, though, ask about the coherence lengh. You can check the coherence length of the laser with a Michaelson by varying the distance of the mirrors from the beamsplitter. As you move one of the mirrors in the interferometer away, the fruinges will eventually lose contrast and finally disappear completely. The distance at which the contrast falls by about 20% is a good measure of coherence.

The polarisatione of the laser will determine the exposure time. In order to get the best possible hologram the object and reference beams must be polarised in the same direction. This is only possible (in a simple setup) with a polarised laser. If the laser is unpolarised (sometimes this is called "randomly polarised"), the brightness wiill decrease from the best possible and/or the exposure times will increase. A polarised laser is not essential, but if you can get one within your budget, it's preferable. It's someting to ask about when you buy. 

If I can be of any further help, you can always email or PM me.

posts.author: tpark
posts.content_md:
Hi,

You can get excellent results with the diode that Intergraf provides - it's not super powerful, but if the stability requirements are met you can get great holograms. If there are problems with your setup, it won't matter how powerful a laser you have, you will still get terrible results.

I purchased a D&S kit, and got the thing assembled, however I had mixed results (mode hopping) with it initially. I modified the circuit so that the drive current could be adjusted, and used the photocell/audio amplifier setup to get it away from a mode hop zone, and I've had good results with that setup. I also have had good results with constant current sources (I bought mine from Ebay for about $30.00). Sealed laser diode modules tend to exhibit mode hopping - I've purchased several from Ebay, and although the device worked fine for producing a bright red spot, there were problems with mode hopping so the output was unsuitable for creating holograms. I've not found any green modules that produce good holograms - I think for that you have to go for a Real Man's laser such as the coherent 315m. I've purchased surplus ebay hene's and they've produced good holograms.

The output from semiconductor lasers tends to be much cleaner than that from the hene, so you can get away without a spatial filter for many setups. 

The mounting for the lasers I purchased from a company called Optima optics. I bought a lot of stuff from Anchor Optical (mirrors and whatnot). If you buy the mountings from Optima, be sure you get the handy laser adjusting tool. 

I agree that Intergraf is very helpful. The service that they provide is first rate.

posts.author: tpark
posts.content_md:
> **Colin Kaminski:** tpark wrote:I purchased a D&S kit, and got the thing assembled, however I had mixed results (mode hopping) with it initially. I modified the circuit so that the drive current could be adjusted, and used the photocell/audio amplifier setup to get it away from a mode hop zone, and I've had good results with that setup.Hi Ted,Can you let me know what exactly you changed?

This is from memory, but I added a potentiometer with Raj (the resistor going from pin 3 to 8 on the chip) - 1k multiturn I think. I'll provide more details when I get home and look at the thing.

Part of the problem with the D&S setup is that it doesn't account for variability between the semiconductor diodes. Mode hops can happen at almost any point in the power/temperature space. That's why using your photocell/amplifier trick is handy - coupled with the added, adjustable resistor, a spot can be found where the device isn't operating in a mode hop zone.

--Ted
